key_claims: Vaccine immunogenicity declines with age due to immunosenescence, underscoring the need for improved adjuvants. LiteVax Adjuvant (LVA), a squalane-in-water emulsion containing carbohydrate fatty-acid monosulphate esters, has shown potential to enhance influenza vaccine responses, but its mechanisms in humans remain unclear. We performed a longitudinal systems vaccinology study in 56 younger (18-45 years) and older ([≥]60 years) adults receiving a quadrivalent influenza vaccine with or without LVA. Multi-omics analyses, including bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, flow cytometry, and serology, revealed that LVA induced a rapid, transient interferon-driven innate response, primarily in monocytes, associated with enhanced antigen processing and dendritic cell to T cell interactions. LVA promoted differentiation of influenza-specific CD4+ T cells toward CD45RO+ memory phenotypes, accelerated early IgG3 antibody responses, and increased IgG-producing plasmablast frequencies without affecting overall antibody magnitude. Importantly, LVA reduced age-related differences in early immune responses, improving response quality and supporting vaccine performance in older adults.
A murine experimental system was developed to manipulate proprioceptive inputs during a memory-dependent localization task in spatial virtual reality.
Bioluminescent optogenetics (luminopsin) was selectively expressed in parvalbumin-positive neurons of the dorsal root ganglia in mice.
The effects of luminopsin last for roughly 20 minutes based on in-vivo IVIS imaging and behavior.
Mice exhibited normal performance in tasks relying on gross motor skills but showed subtle deficits in challenging spatial tasks requiring integration of past movements.
The study provides a first causal demonstration for acute participation of proprioception in path-integration biomechanics.
limitations: The study is a preprint and has not been peer-reviewed.
The effects of luminopsin were only tested for a short duration (roughly 20 minutes).
The study was conducted in mice, and results may not directly translate to humans.
The method for activating opsins with millisecond precision is mentioned as future work, indicating current limitations in temporal precision.
what_not_to_say: The study proves that proprioception is essential for all spatial behaviors.
The study provides a method for human proprioception manipulation.
The study shows that proprioception deficits affect gross motor skills.
The study demonstrates that proprioception is the sole mechanism for path integration.
The study has been peer-reviewed and validated.

key_claims: Critical flicker fusion frequency (CFFF) shows exceptional within-individual stability in adults.
CFFF stability contrasts with the highly plastic spatial abilities processed through the same cortical pathways.
CFFF is unresponsive to non-specific cognitive training but modifiable by perceptual-learning paradigms engaging the magnocellular-dorsal stream.
CFFF may serve as a trait marker, but links to working memory precision, metacognitive accuracy, and capacity limits are testable hypotheses, not established findings.
CFFF emerges from convergent constraints across processing levels.
limitations: The source is an abstract, so details of the review methodology are not provided.
The proposed framework is based on a review, not original empirical data.
The links between CFFF and cognitive traits are hypotheses, not established findings.
what_not_to_say: Do not claim that CFFF is definitively a trait marker for cognitive abilities.
Do not claim that CFFF stability is caused by any single mechanism.
Do not claim that CFFF is completely unmodifiable.
Do not claim that the review provides causal evidence.
